criteria.text: The response identifies that a sale or transfer of more than 50% of the equity of Besouth Holdings Corp. (Besouth's sole member) is an indirect Change of Control of Besouth under the Supply Agreement (Sections 1.3 and 16.2).

The response explains that a Change of Control is deemed an assignment requiring Meideis's prior written consent, and that without that consent Meideis may terminate and demand payment for remaining committed quantities under open Statements of Work.

The response recommends obtaining Meideis's written consent or waiver before any transfer of Holdings' equity closes, and notes that no document in the file, including Amendment No. 1, obtains or waives that consent.

The response calculates that the non-renewal notice deadline under Section 3.2 was on or about October 2, 2026 (180 days before the March 31, 2027 expiry of the Initial Term), and that this deadline had passed by the time Amendment No. 1 was signed on October 20, 2026.

The response concludes that, absent a non-renewal notice, the Supply Agreement will automatically renew for a three-year Renewal Term to about March 31, 2030 with the exclusivity obligation intact, and recommends negotiating a termination right or term change with Meideis.

The response identifies that Amendment No. 1 Section 2.1 replaces the definition of Products, for all purposes of the Agreement, with all architectural glass products that Meideis manufactures, fabricates or supplies, and that this goes beyond the Amendment's stated purpose of adding Calloway spandrel glass.

The response explains that, combined with the Section 5.1 requirement to buy 100% of requirements for Products from Meideis, the new definition extends Besouth's exclusive purchase obligation to all architectural glass on all projects. It also recommends narrowing the definition to add only the Calloway spandrel glass, or carving that glass out of Section 5.1.
The response states that the Supply Agreement became effective April 1, 2023, with a four-year Initial Term.
The response states that Besouth Holdings Corp. is Besouth's sole member and the guarantor under the Parent Guaranty.
The response states that the Calloway Street Tower Statement of Work commits Besouth to 42,000 square feet of insulating glass units.
The response is a memo addressed to the supervising partner that, for each issue, gives the document and section, why it matters for Besouth, and a recommended fix.
The response flags at least one issue as needing to go to the client immediately.
The response fails if it states or implies that Besouth can still give a timely non-renewal notice to avoid the 2027 renewal.
The response fails if it concludes that Besouth's exclusive purchase obligation remains limited to low-E coated insulating glass units after Amendment No. 1.
